graders.name: 01-recall-german-iab
graders.evidence:
There's no open-download worker-firm panel I could find, so nothing you can use for AKM today. All the real options need an application. The fastest ones to get are probably Spain's MCVL and a German SIAB download, and the best long-term fit is German IAB data, if you can get there.

I checked this on 2026-11-12. Registry searches (DataCite, OpenAIRE, Zenodo, Hugging Face) mostly returned noise. The access facts come from web pages I read, and I mark below what I couldn't confirm.

## Options, in the order I'd pursue them

| # | Dataset | Access | Time to access | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Spain – MCVL** (4% sample of Social Security records, with tax earnings) | Paper application to the national Social Security administration, free, no on-site visit | Weeks (my estimate) | Strong, but a small-ish sample |
| 2 | **Germany – SIAB** (2% worker sample, from 1975) | Your institution signs a data use agreement. The downloadable file is the "Regional File". | Weeks to months (my estimate) | Uncertain: I couldn't confirm it carries an establishment ID |
| 3 | **Germany – LIAB / full IAB data** (workers linked to establishments, 1975–2024) | Project proposal, then on-site or remote access only | Months | Strongest for your question |
| 4 | **Italy – INPS** via VisitINPS | 3-month funded visit to Rome | Months | Strong, but the call is competitive |
| 5 | **UK – ASHE** (panel back to 1997, with employer identifiers) | Accredited-researcher route | Months | Good, but survey-based and about 1% of workers |
| 6 | **US – LEHD** | Proposal to a Census Research Data Center | 4–7+ months, longer for non-citizens | Strong, but slowest |
| 7 | **Brazil – RAIS (identified)** | Application to the labor ministry plus an institutional agreement | Unknown | Strong |
| 8 | **Italy – Veneto Worker Histories (VWH)** | Sign a form and email it to the foundation that hosts it | Weeks | Limited: two provinces, 1975–2001 |

**Spain – MCVL.** It has firm identifiers and tax-based earnings that aren't top-coded. Social Security earnings are top- and bottom-coded for about 13% of observations. The process is a stack of Spanish-language forms signed by your institution and sent to the Social Security administration. One replication site (Diego Puga's, [diegopuga.org/data/mcvl](https://diegopuga.org/data/mcvl/)) counted 11 forms, and mentions no fee. I confirmed the process from [the official portal summary](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl) and that site, but not the form count today. Puga's page also has code you could reuse.

**Germany – SIAB.** [The FDZ page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/our-data-products/individual-and-household-data/siab/) confirms that the "factually anonymous" version can be downloaded by applying institutions. The more detailed version is only available during research visits or remote access. You can't use both in one project. A 2023 guide to preparing the SIAB mentions an establishment ID (`betnr`) that is sometimes missing. Check FDZ-Datenreport 07/2023 before you commit.

**Germany – LIAB.** Access is by research visit or remote access only. The 1975–2024 longitudinal model ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.5164/iab.liablm7524.de.en.v1)) provides full employment biographies only for establishments with up to 49 employees. The cross-sectional model may suit you better. Your institution signs a data use agreement, and you must report publications to the FDZ. Foreign researchers are supported (the FDZ has an international access network), but I couldn't confirm PhD-student eligibility.

**Italy – INPS.** [The list of available data](https://www.inps.it/content/dam/inps-site/pdf/datiebilanci/visitinps-scholars/documents/Banche_dati_disponibili-EN.pdf) includes private-sector employer-employee data, annual 1974–2024. Under the Type B call, advanced PhD students (all exams done, thesis pending) can apply. I didn't confirm the current deadline.

**UK – ASHE.** The [UK Data Service secure-access study (SN 6689)](https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/6689) covers 1997–2025. The ONS Secure Research Service also holds ASHE linked to PAYE tax data. I couldn't verify the catalogue page automatically, and I haven't confirmed the employer-ID variable name or whether your institution qualifies.

**US – LEHD.** [The Census page](https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/) confirms that the microdata are restricted to approved projects at Census Research Data Centers. The timeline comes from older RDC slides. Employer-level tax identifiers need extra IRS approval.

**Brazil – RAIS.** The identified version isn't public. Researchers email the labor ministry (`observatoriotrabalho@mte.gov.br`, per the Engbom–Moser replication README). The application needs a project description, a justification for needing person and employer IDs, and an institution that can sign legal agreements.

**Italy – VWH.** [The FRDB page](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/) says to sign the attached form and email it to info@frdb.org. The data end in 2001, and I couldn't confirm a wage variable. It's useful for learning, not for recent inequality trends.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Denmark, Norway and Sweden** have excellent registers. Foreign researchers generally need an affiliation with an approved institution in that country, so a foreign PhD student normally can't apply directly. This is from web summaries, some old.
- **Austria, France (DADS via CASD), Portugal (Quadros de Pessoal), Netherlands (CBS) and Canada (CEEDD)** are from memory only. Each is restricted, and I didn't check them.
- **WHIP (Italy)** is a 1-in-15 sample, 1985–2019, linked to firm data. I couldn't find how to apply.

## Not recommended
- **Arizona UI claimant records** (open, Zenodo) contain unemployment claimants, not an employer-employee wage panel.
- **LODES and QWI** (US Census) are open but aggregated. You can't estimate worker fixed effects from them.
- **Linked Personnel Panel (Germany)** is open to researchers but survey-based and not a wage panel.

## What you can do right now
- Read [*The ABC of AKM*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.17034), a recent user's guide that came up in my search.
- Practise the estimator on simulated data. I believe the `pytwoway` Python package can do this, but I haven't checked it.
- Lock down your cheapest route first (MCVL or SIAB), then ask your advisor which of these your department already has agreements for.

## Next step
A short email to your advisor (do they have contacts at IAB, INPS or Spain's Social Security?) will probably decide this faster than anything else. If you tell me your institution's country and whether you'd travel for a visit, I can narrow this to two options.

The interactive companion page covers only the four sources I formally verified (LIAB, SIAB, VWH, LEHD), not the rest above: `/private/tmp/e-Y0nqy3/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`

graders.evidence:
There's no open-download worker-firm panel I could find, so nothing you can use for AKM today. All the real options need an application. The fastest ones to get are probably Spain's MCVL and a German SIAB download, and the best long-term fit is German IAB data, if you can get there.

I checked this on 2026-11-12. Registry searches (DataCite, OpenAIRE, Zenodo, Hugging Face) mostly returned noise. The access facts come from web pages I read, and I mark below what I couldn't confirm.

## Options, in the order I'd pursue them

| # | Dataset | Access | Time to access | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Spain – MCVL** (4% sample of Social Security records, with tax earnings) | Paper application to the national Social Security administration, free, no on-site visit | Weeks (my estimate) | Strong, but a small-ish sample |
| 2 | **Germany – SIAB** (2% worker sample, from 1975) | Your institution signs a data use agreement. The downloadable file is the "Regional File". | Weeks to months (my estimate) | Uncertain: I couldn't confirm it carries an establishment ID |
| 3 | **Germany – LIAB / full IAB data** (workers linked to establishments, 1975–2024) | Project proposal, then on-site or remote access only | Months | Strongest for your question |
| 4 | **Italy – INPS** via VisitINPS | 3-month funded visit to Rome | Months | Strong, but the call is competitive |
| 5 | **UK – ASHE** (panel back to 1997, with employer identifiers) | Accredited-researcher route | Months | Good, but survey-based and about 1% of workers |
| 6 | **US – LEHD** | Proposal to a Census Research Data Center | 4–7+ months, longer for non-citizens | Strong, but slowest |
| 7 | **Brazil – RAIS (identified)** | Application to the labor ministry plus an institutional agreement | Unknown | Strong |
| 8 | **Italy – Veneto Worker Histories (VWH)** | Sign a form and email it to the foundation that hosts it | Weeks | Limited: two provinces, 1975–2001 |

**Spain – MCVL.** It has firm identifiers and tax-based earnings that aren't top-coded. Social Security earnings are top- and bottom-coded for about 13% of observations. The process is a stack of Spanish-language forms signed by your institution and sent to the Social Security administration. One replication site (Diego Puga's, [diegopuga.org/data/mcvl](https://diegopuga.org/data/mcvl/)) counted 11 forms, and mentions no fee. I confirmed the process from [the official portal summary](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl) and that site, but not the form count today. Puga's page also has code you could reuse.

**Germany – SIAB.** [The FDZ page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/our-data-products/individual-and-household-data/siab/) confirms that the "factually anonymous" version can be downloaded by applying institutions. The more detailed version is only available during research visits or remote access. You can't use both in one project. A 2023 guide to preparing the SIAB mentions an establishment ID (`betnr`) that is sometimes missing. Check FDZ-Datenreport 07/2023 before you commit.

**Germany – LIAB.** Access is by research visit or remote access only. The 1975–2024 longitudinal model ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.5164/iab.liablm7524.de.en.v1)) provides full employment biographies only for establishments with up to 49 employees. The cross-sectional model may suit you better. Your institution signs a data use agreement, and you must report publications to the FDZ. Foreign researchers are supported (the FDZ has an international access network), but I couldn't confirm PhD-student eligibility.

**Italy – INPS.** [The list of available data](https://www.inps.it/content/dam/inps-site/pdf/datiebilanci/visitinps-scholars/documents/Banche_dati_disponibili-EN.pdf) includes private-sector employer-employee data, annual 1974–2024. Under the Type B call, advanced PhD students (all exams done, thesis pending) can apply. I didn't confirm the current deadline.

**UK – ASHE.** The [UK Data Service secure-access study (SN 6689)](https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/6689) covers 1997–2025. The ONS Secure Research Service also holds ASHE linked to PAYE tax data. I couldn't verify the catalogue page automatically, and I haven't confirmed the employer-ID variable name or whether your institution qualifies.

**US – LEHD.** [The Census page](https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/) confirms that the microdata are restricted to approved projects at Census Research Data Centers. The timeline comes from older RDC slides. Employer-level tax identifiers need extra IRS approval.

**Brazil – RAIS.** The identified version isn't public. Researchers email the labor ministry (`observatoriotrabalho@mte.gov.br`, per the Engbom–Moser replication README). The application needs a project description, a justification for needing person and employer IDs, and an institution that can sign legal agreements.

**Italy – VWH.** [The FRDB page](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/) says to sign the attached form and email it to info@frdb.org. The data end in 2001, and I couldn't confirm a wage variable. It's useful for learning, not for recent inequality trends.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Denmark, Norway and Sweden** have excellent registers. Foreign researchers generally need an affiliation with an approved institution in that country, so a foreign PhD student normally can't apply directly. This is from web summaries, some old.
- **Austria, France (DADS via CASD), Portugal (Quadros de Pessoal), Netherlands (CBS) and Canada (CEEDD)** are from memory only. Each is restricted, and I didn't check them.
- **WHIP (Italy)** is a 1-in-15 sample, 1985–2019, linked to firm data. I couldn't find how to apply.

## Not recommended
- **Arizona UI claimant records** (open, Zenodo) contain unemployment claimants, not an employer-employee wage panel.
- **LODES and QWI** (US Census) are open but aggregated. You can't estimate worker fixed effects from them.
- **Linked Personnel Panel (Germany)** is open to researchers but survey-based and not a wage panel.

## What you can do right now
- Read [*The ABC of AKM*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.17034), a recent user's guide that came up in my search.
- Practise the estimator on simulated data. I believe the `pytwoway` Python package can do this, but I haven't checked it.
- Lock down your cheapest route first (MCVL or SIAB), then ask your advisor which of these your department already has agreements for.

## Next step
A short email to your advisor (do they have contacts at IAB, INPS or Spain's Social Security?) will probably decide this faster than anything else. If you tell me your institution's country and whether you'd travel for a visit, I can narrow this to two options.

The interactive companion page covers only the four sources I formally verified (LIAB, SIAB, VWH, LEHD), not the rest above: `/private/tmp/e-Y0nqy3/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`

I confirmed the process from [the official portal summary](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl) and that site, but not the form count today. Puga's page also has code you could reuse.

**Germany – SIAB.** [The FDZ page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/our-data-products/individual-and-household-data/siab/) confirms that the "factually anonymous" version can be downloaded by applying institutions. The more detailed version is only available during research visits or remote access. You can't use both in one project. A 2023 guide to preparing the SIAB mentions an establishment ID (`betnr`) that is sometimes missing. Check FDZ-Datenreport 07/2023 before you commit.

**Germany – LIAB.** Access is by research visit or remote access only. The 1975–2024 longitudinal model ([DOI](https://doi.org/10.5164/iab.liablm7524.de.en.v1)) provides full employment biographies only for establishments with up to 49 employees. The cross-sectional model may suit you better. Your institution signs a data use agreement, and you must report publications to the FDZ. Foreign researchers are supported (the FDZ has an international access network), but I couldn't confirm PhD-student eligibility.

**Italy – INPS.** [The list of available data](https://www.inps.it/content/dam/inps-site/pdf/datiebilanci/visitinps-scholars/documents/Banche_dati_disponibili-EN.pdf) includes private-sector employer-employee data, annual 1974–2024. Under the Type B call, advanced PhD students (all exams done, thesis pending) can apply. I didn't confirm the current deadline.

**UK – ASHE.** The [UK Data Service secure-access study (SN 6689)](https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/6689) covers 1997–2025. The ONS Secure Research Service also holds ASHE linked to PAYE tax data. I couldn't verify the catalogue page automatically, and I haven't confirmed the employer-ID variable name or whether your institution qualifies.

**US – LEHD.** [The Census page](https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/) confirms that the microdata are restricted to approved projects at Census Research Data Centers. The timeline comes from older RDC slides. Employer-level tax identifiers need extra IRS approval.

**Brazil – RAIS.** The identified version isn't public. Researchers email the labor ministry (`observatoriotrabalho@mte.gov.br`, per the Engbom–Moser replication README). The application needs a project description, a justification for needing person and employer IDs, and an institution that can sign legal agreements.

**Italy – VWH.** [The FRDB page](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/) says to sign the attached form and email it to info@frdb.org. The data end in 2001, and I couldn't confirm a wage variable. It's useful for learning, not for recent inequality trends.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Denmark, Norway and Sweden** have excellent registers. Foreign researchers generally need an affiliation with an approved institution in that country, so a foreign PhD student normally can't apply directly. This is from web summaries, some old.
- **Austria, France (DADS via CASD), Portugal (Quadros de Pessoal), Netherlands (CBS) and Canada (CEEDD)** are from memory only. Each is restricted, and I didn't check them.
- **WHIP (Italy)** is a 1-in-15 sample, 1985–2019, linked to firm data. I couldn't find how to apply.

## Not recommended
- **Arizona UI claimant records** (open, Zenodo) contain unemployment claimants, not an employer-employee wage panel.
- **LODES and QWI** (US Census) are open but aggregated. You can't estimate worker fixed effects from them.
- **Linked Personnel Panel (Germany)** is open to researchers but survey-based and not a wage panel.

## What you can do right now
- Read [*The ABC of AKM*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.17034), a recent user's guide that came up in my search.
- Practise the estimator on simulated data. I believe the `pytwoway` Python package can do this, but I haven't checked it.
- Lock down your cheapest route first (MCVL or SIAB), then ask your advisor which of these your department already has agreements for.

## Next step
A short email to your advisor (do they have contacts at IAB, INPS or Spain's Social Security?) will probably decide this faster than anything else. If you tell me your institution's country and whether you'd travel for a visit, I can narrow this to two options.

The interactive companion page covers only the four sources I formally verified (LIAB, SIAB, VWH, LEHD), not the rest above: `/private/tmp/e-Y0nqy3/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`

## What I assumed you need

- **R1 (must):** worker-level earnings followed over 10 or more years.
- **R2 (must):** an employer ID on each job spell, so job movers can be tracked. AKM needs a connected set of firms linked by movers.
- **R3 (must):** a long span that covers the rise in inequality.
- **R4 (nice to have):** a real wage measure (daily or annual earnings), not just contribution bases.
- I assumed you can wait weeks to months, and that you may be outside the country whose data you use. That second point matters a lot for access.

I checked on 2026-11-12. I also ran registry searches on DataCite, OpenAIRE, Zenodo and Hugging Face.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Germany: IAB SIAB (2% sample of social-security biographies, 1975 on) | Data Use Agreement. The scientific-use file (Regional File 7523) is downloadable by applying institutions. The less anonymised version is on-site or remote only. About weeks. | FDZ terms; you must report publications within one month | Strong | FDZ page today; establishment ID in the SUF not confirmed |
| 2 | Germany: IAB LIAB longitudinal model 1975–2024 | Application, Data Usage Agreement, on-site or remote use. About months. | FDZ terms | Strong | Today |
| 3 | Spain: MCVL (4% sample, firm contribution-account IDs) | Request forms approved by the social security directorate (DGOSS). No fee reported. About weeks. | Accessibility agreement | Strong | Search summary and portal link; forms not read |
| 4 | Italy: Veneto Workers Histories (VWH), 1975–2001 | Signed form emailed to info@frdb.org. | Must cite the source | Partial | Page read today |
| 5 | US: LEHD microdata | Federal Statistical Research Data Center proposal. About 6–12+ months. | Census Special Sworn Status | Strong | Search summary |
| 6 | Germany: SIAB Campus File (7508) | Free after registering and accepting the terms. Minutes. | Teaching use only | Weak, for practice only | Today |

## Details

**1. SIAB** ([FDZ page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/our-data-products/individual-and-household-data/siab/))
- **Contents:** a 2% random sample of the IEB, German social-security employment records from 1975.
- **Why it fits:** it is the standard scientific-use dataset for AKM-type work on Germany. Sample size is thinner than LIAB or the full IEB.
- **Gaps:**
  - A guide to the 7519 version names the establishment variable `betnr`. I could not confirm that the Regional File (the downloadable version) keeps it, so check its data report before applying.
  - Wages are top-coded at the social-security ceiling, from memory.
  - The weakly anonymous and Regional File versions cannot both be used in one project.
- **If you are in the US:** FDZ says extra restrictions apply to access from the US. The page I read did not say what they are. Check the IDAN (International Data Access Network) page.

**2. LIAB** ([FDZ record](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/linked-employer-employee-data-of-the-iab-liab-liab-longitudinal-model-1975-2024-version-1/))
- **Contents:** employee histories linked to the IAB Establishment Panel survey.
- **Limits:** the page says full employment biographies are provided only for establishments with up to 49 employees. It covers establishments in the survey panel, not all firms.
- **Best use:** if you want firm covariates (collective bargaining, investment) next to the decomposition.

**3. MCVL** ([portal](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl))
- **Contents:** a 4% sample of everyone with a Social Security relationship in the reference year, with full histories.
- **Access:** you download the request form and a researcher form, and DGOSS approves. One researcher page mentions about 11 forms when tax data are included, and an older source says files were sent on DVD. Both may be outdated.
- **Gaps:** earnings are contribution bases with top and bottom coding, from memory. A usable code reference is [Puga's MCVL code](https://diegopuga.org/data/mcvl/).

**4. VWH** ([FRDB](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/))

- **Limits:** it ends in 2001 and covers one region, so it is useful for method work but not for recent inequality trends.

**5. LEHD**
- **Access:** you need a proposal through a Federal Statistical Research Data Center (FSRDC), Special Sworn Status, and in some cases SSA and IRS approval.
- **Timing:** proposal development takes 6–12 months or more. Output must come from a sample of at least three states.
- **Public alternatives:** QWI, J2J and LODES are public but aggregated, so they cannot support AKM.

- It is "specifically designed for the purpose of academic teaching". FDZ says only the scientific-use file supports real analysis. Use it to build your pipeline, not to produce results.

## Known, not confirmed

- **Denmark, Norway and Sweden** have the best-known worker-firm registers. A search summary says Statistics Denmark authorises research environments rather than individuals. Non-residents need a link to an approved Danish institution, and work happens on its servers. Norway and Sweden are similar, with some older sources. Check each statistics office's current rules.
- **Brazil's RAIS** (the Ministry of Labor's annual worker-firm register) has identified microdata. A 2026 PNAS paper says you apply to the Ministry. Non-identified microdata are public. I recall the public version lacks a usable worker ID, but I did not verify that.
- **Portugal (Quadros de Pessoal), France (DADS panel) and Canada (CEEDD)** are used in published AKM work. I did not check any of their access terms.

## Not recommended

- **US QWI, J2J and LODES:** public but aggregated, with no worker IDs, so they cannot support AKM.
- **The registry hits for "linked employer-employee" apart from IAB:** these were replication files and unrelated records.

## What I could not find

I found no open download that has both worker IDs and employer IDs over 10 or more years. If one exists, it is not in the registries I searched. Everything usable for real estimates needs a signed agreement or an application.

## Next step

**Today:**
- Register for the SIAB Campus File and build your AKM pipeline on it: connected set, a high-dimensional fixed effects estimator, and a bias correction for limited mobility.
- Read the Regional File data report to confirm the establishment ID.
- Email info@frdb.org for VWH.

**Parallel track:**
- If you are at a German or other institution with a FDZ-IAB agreement, start the SIAB application.
- If Spain or Italy fits your question, request the MCVL.
- Ask your advisor which datacentre arrangements your department already has. That often decides between the national datasets above.

Sources: [FDZ SIAB](https://fdz.iab.de/en/our-data-products/individual-and-household-data/siab/), [FDZ LIAB](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/linked-employer-employee-data-of-the-iab-liab-liab-longitudinal-model-1975-2024-version-1/), [MCVL portal](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl), [FRDB VWH](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/), [LEHD data](https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/), [FSRDC guidelines](https://www2.census.gov/adrm/FSRDC/Apply_For_Access/Research_Proposal_Guidelines.pdf), [Statistics Denmark access](https://www.dst.dk/ext/5452354440/0/israel2016/Annex-B5-15-Introduction-to-the-Danish-system-for-access-to-microdata--pdf).

graders.evidence:
## What I assumed you need

- **R1 (must):** worker-level earnings followed over 10 or more years.
- **R2 (must):** an employer ID on each job spell, so job movers can be tracked. AKM needs a connected set of firms linked by movers.
- **R3 (must):** a long span that covers the rise in inequality.
- **R4 (nice to have):** a real wage measure (daily or annual earnings), not just contribution bases.
- I assumed you can wait weeks to months, and that you may be outside the country whose data you use. That second point matters a lot for access.

I checked on 2026-11-12. I also ran registry searches on DataCite, OpenAIRE, Zenodo and Hugging Face.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Germany: IAB SIAB (2% sample of social-security biographies, 1975 on) | Data Use Agreement. The scientific-use file (Regional File 7523) is downloadable by applying institutions. The less anonymised version is on-site or remote only. About weeks. | FDZ terms; you must report publications within one month | Strong | FDZ page today; establishment ID in the SUF not confirmed |
| 2 | Germany: IAB LIAB longitudinal model 1975–2024 | Application, Data Usage Agreement, on-site or remote use. About months. | FDZ terms | Strong | Today |
| 3 | Spain: MCVL (4% sample, firm contribution-account IDs) | Request forms approved by the social security directorate (DGOSS). No fee reported. About weeks. | Accessibility agreement | Strong | Search summary and portal link; forms not read |
| 4 | Italy: Veneto Workers Histories (VWH), 1975–2001 | Signed form emailed to info@frdb.org. | Must cite the source | Partial | Page read today |
| 5 | US: LEHD microdata | Federal Statistical Research Data Center proposal. About 6–12+ months. | Census Special Sworn Status | Strong | Search summary |
| 6 | Germany: SIAB Campus File (7508) | Free after registering and accepting the terms. Minutes. | Teaching use only | Weak, for practice only | Today |

## Details

**1. SIAB** ([FDZ page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/our-data-products/individual-and-household-data/siab/))
- **Contents:** a 2% random sample of the IEB, German social-security employment records from 1975.
- **Why it fits:** it is the standard scientific-use dataset for AKM-type work on Germany. Sample size is thinner than LIAB or the full IEB.
- **Gaps:**
  - A guide to the 7519 version names the establishment variable `betnr`. I could not confirm that the Regional File (the downloadable version) keeps it, so check its data report before applying.
  - Wages are top-coded at the social-security ceiling, from memory.
  - The weakly anonymous and Regional File versions cannot both be used in one project.
- **If you are in the US:** FDZ says extra restrictions apply to access from the US. The page I read did not say what they are. Check the IDAN (International Data Access Network) page.

**2. LIAB** ([FDZ record](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/linked-employer-employee-data-of-the-iab-liab-liab-longitudinal-model-1975-2024-version-1/))
- **Contents:** employee histories linked to the IAB Establishment Panel survey.
- **Limits:** the page says full employment biographies are provided only for establishments with up to 49 employees. It covers establishments in the survey panel, not all firms.
- **Best use:** if you want firm covariates (collective bargaining, investment) next to the decomposition.

**3. MCVL** ([portal](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl))
- **Contents:** a 4% sample of everyone with a Social Security relationship in the reference year, with full histories.
- **Access:** you download the request form and a researcher form, and DGOSS approves. One researcher page mentions about 11 forms when tax data are included, and an older source says files were sent on DVD. Both may be outdated.
- **Gaps:** earnings are contribution bases with top and bottom coding, from memory. A usable code reference is [Puga's MCVL code](https://diegopuga.org/data/mcvl/).

**4. VWH** ([FRDB](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/))
- **Access:** fill in a form and email it to info@frdb.org. The page does not say who is eligible, the conditions or the time to access, and it does not mention a wage variable.
- **Limits:** it ends in 2001 and covers one region, so it is useful for method work but not for recent inequality trends.

**5. LEHD**
- **Access:** you need a proposal through a Federal Statistical Research Data Center (FSRDC), Special Sworn Status, and in some cases SSA and IRS approval.
- **Timing:** proposal development takes 6–12 months or more. Output must come from a sample of at least three states.
- **Public alternatives:** QWI, J2J and LODES are public but aggregated, so they cannot support AKM.

**6. SIAB Campus File** ([FDZ page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/pd_hd/campus-file-sample-of-integrated-labour-market-biographies-siab-cf-7508/))
- It is "specifically designed for the purpose of academic teaching". FDZ says only the scientific-use file supports real analysis. Use it to build your pipeline, not to produce results.

## Known, not confirmed

- **Denmark, Norway and Sweden** have the best-known worker-firm registers. A search summary says Statistics Denmark authorises research environments rather than individuals. Non-residents need a link to an approved Danish institution, and work happens on its servers. Norway and Sweden are similar, with some older sources. Check each statistics office's current rules.
- **Brazil's RAIS** (the Ministry of Labor's annual worker-firm register) has identified microdata. A 2026 PNAS paper says you apply to the Ministry. Non-identified microdata are public. I recall the public version lacks a usable worker ID, but I did not verify that.
- **Portugal (Quadros de Pessoal), France (DADS panel) and Canada (CEEDD)** are used in published AKM work. I did not check any of their access terms.

## Not recommended

- **US QWI, J2J and LODES:** public but aggregated, with no worker IDs, so they cannot support AKM.
- **The registry hits for "linked employer-employee" apart from IAB:** these were replication files and unrelated records.

## What I could not find

I found no open download that has both worker IDs and employer IDs over 10 or more years. If one exists, it is not in the registries I searched. Everything usable for real estimates needs a signed agreement or an application.

**Today:**
- Register for the SIAB Campus File and build your AKM pipeline on it: connected set, a high-dimensional fixed effects estimator, and a bias correction for limited mobility.
- Read the Regional File data report to confirm the establishment ID.
- Email info@frdb.org for VWH.

- If Spain or Italy fits your question, request the MCVL.
- Ask your advisor which datacentre arrangements your department already has. That often decides between the national datasets above.

graders.name: 01-recall-german-iab
graders.evidence:
I haven't checked any of the access terms below against current websites. Application rules and fees change, so confirm each one with the data provider before you plan around it.

## Access options, from most to least realistic for a PhD student

| Source | Coverage | What access takes | Realistic timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Portugal: Quadros de Pessoal** (via Banco de Portugal's BPLIM) | Annual census of private-sector employers and employees, with worker, firm and wage data. Hours are included, and it has been used for well-known AKM papers. | Project proposal and institutional affiliation. Work runs in a remote environment. As I remember it, BPLIM is open to external and foreign academics, but check this. | Weeks to a few months |
| **Germany: IAB (SIAB, LIAB, full IEB)** | Social security records going back decades. | The SIAB scientific-use file (a 2% sample of individuals) needs a data-use contract signed by your institution. LIAB and the full data need remote execution (JoSuA) or an on-site visit in Nuremberg. | SIAB: weeks to months. Full data: months |
| **France: DADS (via CASD)** | Matched employer-employee panel. | The statistical-secrecy committee approves your project. Access is through a secure physical terminal or remote box, and there are fees. Foreign researchers are eligible. | 3–6+ months |
| **Italy: INPS (VisitINPS Scholars)** | Social security worker-firm data. | Competitive program aimed at PhD students and early-career researchers. The program has historically involved a stay at INPS. | One application cycle, then the program length |
| **US: Census LEHD** (through an FSRDC) | Quarterly earnings, linked workers and employers. | Proposal approval, Special Sworn Status and a background check. Residency and citizenship rules can be a barrier for non-US persons. Earnings are quarterly, with no hours. | 6–12+ months |
| **US: state UI wage records** | Same structure as LEHD, for one state. | In practice this means a coauthor with an existing agreement with the state agency. | Depends entirely on the relationship |
| **Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland** | Excellent, near-complete registers, which are the gold standard. | Access is generally through a national institution. This usually means a Danish, Swedish or Norwegian affiliation or a local coauthor, and it is much harder as a foreign student. | Months, with the affiliation as the real barrier |
| **Brazil: RAIS identified, Hungary: Admin3** | Both have been used for AKM work. | Both are access-by-agreement. For Brazil, I'm unsure what is public and what isn't. | Unclear |

Two data caveats matter for your question:
- **Germany:** wages are top-coded at the social security ceiling. This directly affects inequality measures, so you would need an imputation step, as Card, Heining and Kline did. The SIAB is a worker sample, so it covers few workers per firm. Firm effects will be noisy and the connected set thin. The full data or LIAB are better for AKM.
- **US:** LEHD has no hours, so you can't separate wage rates from hours.

## What you can start on now

I don't know of any open dataset with real linked worker-firm histories. Here is what you can do in the meantime:

1. **Build and test your pipeline on simulated data.** You can write and debug the whole estimation and decomposition code now:
   - Estimate with `reghdfe` (Stata), `pyfixest` or `lfe`.
   - Use `pytwoway` (Python), which includes a data simulator and bias-correction tools.
   - Correct for limited-mobility bias with Kline-Saggio-Sølvsten leave-one-out code.
   - Restrict to the largest connected set.
   - Decompose the change in wage variance into worker, firm and sorting terms, plus the within/between split.
2. **Read the replication packages.** These include Card-Heining-Kline (Germany), Song et al. "Firming Up Inequality" (US), and the Brazil and Portugal papers. They show the exact sample restrictions and decomposition formulas.
3. **Use public aggregates for preliminary descriptives.** US QWI and LODES can't support AKM. They can give you rough between-industry or between-firm-size patterns while you wait.
4. **Look at the Veneto Workers History (Italy).** I believe it has been shared with researchers on request, with much lighter access requirements. I'm not sure it's currently available, so email the maintainers.

## What I'd do

1. Ask your advisor whether the department already has a data agreement, or whether any coauthor does. This is often faster than any application.
2. Apply to **BPLIM (Portugal)** and the **IAB SIAB** in parallel. They are the most accessible for a foreign student, and both have long panels. Add the **VisitINPS** program if the cycle fits.
3. Build your pipeline on simulated data while you wait.

If you'd like, I can write the simulated-data pipeline (AKM estimation, connected set, KSS correction, variance decomposition) in Python or Stata. I can also pull current application pages for BPLIM and IAB, if web access works in this session.

graders.name: 01-recall-german-iab
graders.evidence:
**Short answer:** nothing with real worker and employer IDs is freely downloadable today. The most realistic routes for a PhD student are Portugal, Spain, Italy (VisitINPS) and the Netherlands. The US and Nordic countries are much slower. I'm working from memory and haven't checked current rules, so confirm each one with the data provider before you plan around it. The timelines are rough estimates.

## Options with realistic access for a PhD student

| Data | Coverage | What access takes | Caveats |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Portugal, Quadros de Pessoal** (Banco de Portugal BPLIM) | Full population of private-sector firms and workers, 1980s to about 2020 | Apply with a project description, an institutional affiliation and a supervisor. You can work through BPLIM's remote-access system, and I believe non-Portuguese researchers are eligible. Expect weeks to a few months. | It's a well-studied AKM setting, which helps with benchmarking and referees. Check BPLIM's current fees and rules. |
| **Spain, MCVL** (Social Security sample) | 4% sample of Social Security affiliates, from 2004 | Apply to the Social Security ministry with a project description and institutional support. I believe it's free and the files are delivered to you, but I'm not certain. | A 4% sample means few co-workers per firm and a small connected set. That makes mobility bias worse and weakens the firm-level part of the decomposition. |
| **Italy, VisitINPS Scholars** | Full INPS matched employer-employee records | A competitive call. You work on-site at INPS in Rome for a fixed period, and the program is aimed at PhD students and early-career researchers. | You have to be physically present, and it depends on the call timing. |
| **Netherlands, CBS microdata** | Full population, including job spells linked to firms | Remote access through an authorized institution, usually via a supervisor's contract. Fees apply unless your institution is covered. | Can take months to set up. |
| **Germany, IAB** | SIAB: 2% sample. LIAB: linked establishment data. | The FDZ requires a data-use contract and, for some products, remote execution. Allow a few months. | SIAB has the same sampling problem as the Spanish data. The full-population versions are much harder to get. |

## Hard to get as an outsider

- **US LEHD / Census FSRDC:** You need a proposal, a Census benefit justification and Special Sworn Status with a background check. Expect 6 to 18 months, and it's only practical if your institution hosts an FSRDC. Some state UI wage-record data exist, but each state sets its own terms.
- **Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland:** The data are excellent. Access usually requires a local institution or co-author, and sometimes you must be physically in the country. Finland has been more open to remote access from abroad, but verify that.
- **France (DADS via CASD) and Brazil (RAIS):** Both are possible, but they involve long approval processes, and the identified RAIS data need an agreement with the ministry. The public RAIS files, as far as I know, don't have the worker and firm IDs you need.

## What you can start on this week

1. **Build and test the estimation pipeline on simulated data.** Use `pytwoway` (Python, from Bonhomme, Lamadon and Manresa). It simulates matched data and implements the AKM fixed-effects, bias-corrected and group-based estimators. Also look at the KSS leave-one-out code from Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten, and `reghdfe` or `fixest` for high-dimensional fixed effects.
2. **Write your decomposition code now.** Whatever data you end up with, you'll need within- versus between-firm variance by year, the variance of worker effects, firm effects and their covariance by period, and the connected-set restrictions. Debugging it on synthetic data saves months.
3. **Use public aggregate data for context.** LEHD's LODES and Job-to-Job Flows are free, but they have no worker IDs, so they can't support AKM. They are useful for motivating figures and for the descriptive between-firm story.
4. **Start the applications now.** I'd begin with Portugal and, in parallel, a Spanish MCVL request or a VisitINPS application. They have different timelines, so applying to several costs little.

## Methodological notes

- With sampled data (MCVL, SIAB), the connected set is small and the leave-one-out connected set is smaller. Plug-in AKM variance estimates are biased by limited mobility, so budget for bias correction.
- Your 10-year requirement is easy to meet with the full-population datasets above. Check that the sample period includes the inequality rise you care about. Portugal's data cover a long span, and the German and Italian data cover more than that.
- A pure within- versus between-firm variance decomposition doesn't need AKM. AKM is what lets you split the between-firm part into sorting and pay premiums. Your supervisor may want both.

I can look up the current application pages and deadlines for any of these if you tell me which two or three you want to pursue.

graders.name: 01-recall-german-iab
graders.evidence:
I answered this from memory without checking live sources, and access rules change often. Confirm each item on the data provider's page before you plan around it.

## Short answer

Nothing is both usable for AKM and downloadable today without an application. Linked employer-employee data with worker-level job histories is essentially always restricted. The realistic fast options need an application that takes weeks to a few months, not years.

## Accessible to an individual PhD student (weeks to months)

| Data | Country, years | What it takes | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SIAB** (IAB, FDZ) | Germany, 1975 to about 2020 | Application and data-use contract with FDZ-IAB. Academic use is cheap. Access is by remote execution or a scientific-use file, depending on the version. | It's a 2% sample of workers, so you get thin mobility per firm and a smaller connected set. **LIAB** (linked to the establishment survey) is better for firms but more restricted. |
| **MCVL** (Social Security) | Spain, 2005 to present, with histories back further | Application to the Spanish Social Security administration with a research justification. I believe it's open to foreign academics, but check. | It's a 4% sample, so the same thin-mobility issue. Earnings are based on contribution bases, which are capped. |
| **Admin3** (KRTK Databank) | Hungary, 2003 to 2017 | Request through the Databank. This is often the easiest full-population-style linked dataset for outsiders. | Hungary is a less standard setting for the inequality question, and I'm unsure about current access terms. |
| **VisitINPS Scholars / Veneto Workers History** | Italy | VisitINPS is a competitive program that is aimed partly at PhD students and involves visiting INPS. VWH is a regional dataset obtained by agreement with its custodians. | Selective, and the visit may require relocation. |

Germany is probably the best first target. It has the longest panel, a large AKM literature (Card, Heining and Kline 2013) to benchmark against, and a clear process. Mobility bias is the issue to plan around with a sample that thin.

## Needs a local institution, a coauthor, or a long process

- **Nordic countries (Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland):** These have excellent full-population data. Access usually requires affiliation with an authorized domestic institution or a local coauthor, plus fees and a project approval. A visiting-researcher stay or a coauthor makes this feasible.
- **Netherlands (CBS), France (DADS via CASD), Austria, Portugal (Quadros de Pessoal):** These are all possible but typically need a national partner and ethics or secrecy-committee approval. Expect months.
- **United States (Census LEHD via FSRDC):** This takes a proposal, Special Sworn Status and a background check. It can take a year or more from proposal to data, and the project must fit Census's benefit criteria. State UI wage records are sometimes more tractable through a faculty member's existing agreement. Several landmark within/between papers use restricted US data.
- **UK (ONS Secure Research Service, ASHE linked to firm identifiers):** This requires researcher accreditation and project approval, and the data is sample-based.
- **Brazil (RAIS):** I recall the worker-identified file being restricted. Check whether the public version on Base dos Dados has a usable worker ID. I suspect it doesn't.

## What you can do right now

1. **Ask your advisor and department.** Faculty or senior students often already hold access or agreements, and a coauthor with data is often the fastest route.
2. **Build the pipeline on simulated data.** Writing it while your application is pending avoids dead time. Use Python `pytwoway` (Bonhomme–Lamadon–Manresa and AKM tools), Stata `reghdfe`, or R `lfe`/`fixest`.
3. **Learn the bias corrections now.** Limited-mobility bias inflates the firm-effect variance and distorts the covariance in AKM variance decompositions. Kline–Saggio–Sølvsten leave-out estimators and BLM grouped fixed effects are standard fixes, and they matter more with sampled data like SIAB or MCVL.
4. **Replicate the method from replication packages.** Many papers post code even when the data is restricted.
5. **Use aggregate public data for context only.** US LODES, QWI and J2J are not usable for AKM because they have no individual worker histories.

## My suggestion

Apply to FDZ-IAB for SIAB and to Spain's MCVL in parallel, since both are real, relatively fast paths. At the same time, ask your advisor about a Nordic coauthor or visit if you want full-population data. Start with Germany for the first draft. If you tell me which country or institution you're based in, I can narrow this down. I can also look up current application pages if you want them verified.

graders.name: 01-recall-ami-meetings
graders.evidence:
## What I assumed you need
- **Must-haves:** real (non-simulated) English multi-party meetings, speaker-turn annotations, and a licence that permits commercial use. A paid licence is fine.
- **Nice-to-haves:** far-field or microphone-array audio, and business-style content.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **AMI Meeting Corpus** | Direct download, minutes | CC BY 4.0, commercial use OK | Strong | Licence and download page read today |
| 2 | **NOTSOFAR-1** (recorded meetings) | Download via the repo or Hugging Face, minutes | CC BY 4.0 per the GitHub banner; the dataset page shows none | Strong, pending licence check | Partly today |
| 3 | **ICSI Meeting Speech and Transcripts** (LDC2004S02, LDC2004T04) | Paid LDC order, days | LDC user agreement; commercial terms not read | Good, pending licence check | LDC pages seen today |
| 4 | **DiPCo** | Zenodo download | CDLA-Permissive-1.0 | Weak | Registry record confirmed today |

## Details
- **AMI** (https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/corpus/)
  - It has about 100 hours of meetings recorded with an 8-channel circular array plus headset mics. The manual annotations include speaker segments. The array and size details are from memory.
  - The licence page says it "and its annotations are released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license". You need to give attribution.
  - Roughly two thirds of the meetings are scenario role-play: participants act a design team. The page says "different roles in a design team". The rest are natural meetings. That is the main caveat on "real".
  - Download: https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/download/
- **NOTSOFAR-1** (https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge)
  - It is a Microsoft distant-meeting benchmark with real recorded office meetings and multi-device far-field audio. It is also built for diarization plus transcription. The real-versus-simulated split and the annotation details beyond the repo README are from memory.
  - The repo banner says "MIT, CC-BY-4.0 licenses found", but the Hugging Face record states no licence. Read the dataset card or ask Microsoft before relying on it.
  - It also includes a roughly 1,000-hour simulated training set. Leave that out if you need real audio only.
  - Of everything I found, this is the closest match to your far-field and business-meeting needs. It is also the most recent.
- **ICSI** (https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S02)
  - It has about 75 hours of naturally occurring research-group meetings with far-field tabletop microphones, from memory.
  - The LDC page says "Login for the applicable fee". I did not read the non-member agreement's commercial clause, so check that before buying.
  - It is academic group talk rather than business meetings.
- **DiPCo** (https://zenodo.org/records/8122551)
  - It has real far-field array recordings, but of dinner parties, and it is small. Use it only for far-field robustness testing.

## Known, not confirmed
These are from memory and I did not check them this session. Treat each as something to look up, not as a recommendation.
- Other LDC meeting corpora, such as the NIST Rich Transcription meeting sets and ISL. I saw their LDC records but did not read their terms. They are older and mostly overlap with ICSI and AMI.
- ICSI may also be distributed openly outside LDC. I could not confirm that.

## Not recommended, and why
- **MeetingBank audio** is CC BY-NC-SA, so it is non-commercial.
- **ELITR Minuting Corpus** is CC BY-NC-SA.
- **ground-truth/multichannel-meetings-10h** is CC BY-NC.
- **CHiME-6** is dinner parties.
- **AliMeeting and AISHELL-4** are Mandarin.

## What I could not find
- No open, commercial-use corpus of real, unscripted business meetings with far-field audio exists at scale beyond NOTSOFAR-1, so you may eventually need to record your own.
- The literature search returned little useful, and the Hugging Face search partly failed because the response was too large. The list may be incomplete.

## Next step
1. Download AMI today.
2. Confirm NOTSOFAR's data licence in writing, then use its recorded meetings for far-field work.
3. Read the LDC non-member terms before paying for ICSI.
4. Have counsel confirm the CC BY attribution requirements for a commercial product.

I checked all of this on 2026-11-11. The companion page is at `/private/tmp/e-9FYM0L/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

  - **What it contains:** real meetings recorded on multi-channel array devices, built for distant diarization plus ASR. The paper is "NOTSOFAR-1 Challenge: New Datasets, Baseline, and Tasks for Distant Meeting Transcription" (2024).
  - **Licence:** GitHub shows "MIT, CC-BY-4.0 licenses found", but the registry gave no licence for the data. Check the dataset card before you ship.

- **AMI:**

- **ICSI:**
  - **What it contains:** real research-group meetings. The [page](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/icsi/) says the signals, transcripts and some annotations were released under CC BY 4.0. The page describes close-talking microphones. Table-top far-field mics are from memory.
  - **Caution:** the meetings are academic, not business.
- **DiPCo:**
  - **What it contains:** real four-person conversations captured by five 7-mic far-field arrays.
  - **Caution:** it is a dinner-party setting, so it fits your array need but not "business meetings".
- **NIST RT / LDC:**
  - **What it contains:** classic meeting evaluation sets, with a per-corpus LDC fee (the LDC page says "Login for the applicable fee").
  - **Caution:** LDC non-member terms are often research-oriented, so ask LDC in writing about commercial use. I couldn't confirm this.

## Known, not confirmed
- **CHiME-6 / CHiME-5:** the data page returned 404. From memory the licence is non-commercial, so treat it as excluded unless you confirm otherwise.

## Not recommended
- **MeetingBank:** CC BY-NC-SA, and it is city-council data.
- **ground-truth/multichannel-meetings-10h:** CC BY-NC.
- **DIHARD (LDC):** mixed domains and a fee, not meeting-focused.

## What I could not find
No large, commercially licensed corpus of real business meetings with far-field audio exists in what I searched. The Hugging Face search partly failed, and the registries returned a lot of noise. For production-scale data you would likely need to record and license your own, or negotiate with a commercial speech-data vendor.

Start with NOTSOFAR-1's real-meeting subsets and AMI today, and confirm the NOTSOFAR dataset-card licence. Checked 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12. Interactive page: `dataset-shortlist.html`.

graders.name: 01-recall-ami-meetings
graders.evidence:
## What I assumed you need

- **R1 (must):** real, not simulated, multi-party English conversation.
- **R2 (must):** who-spoke-when annotations.
- **R3 (must):** commercial use allowed. A paid licence is fine; research-only and non-commercial data is out.
- **R4 (nice to have):** business-style meetings.
- **R5 (nice to have):** far-field or microphone-array audio.

I checked on 2026-11-12. The literature search returned nothing useful, so the list comes from the registries plus what I already knew.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NOTSOFAR-1 recorded meetings (Microsoft) | Direct download, minutes | CC BY 4.0 per the GitHub repo; the Hugging Face record states none | Strong | Partly: repo licence read today, Hugging Face licence missing |
| 2 | AMI Meeting Corpus | Direct download, minutes | CC BY 4.0 | Strong, but scenario-driven | Today |
| 3 | DiPCo (Dinner Party Corpus) | Direct download, minutes | CDLA-Permissive-1.0 | Partial: informal setting | Today |
| 4 | ICSI Meeting Speech and Transcripts (LDC) | LDC account and fee, days | LDC non-member agreement | Partial, commercial terms unconfirmed | Today |

## Details

**1. NOTSOFAR-1** ([GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge), [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/microsoft/NOTSOFAR))
- **Content:** real meetings in office conference rooms, recorded with several multi-microphone array devices and single-channel devices. It was built for a distant diarization and ASR challenge.
- **Real versus simulated:** the dataset also includes a roughly 1,000-hour simulated training set. Use only the recorded-meeting part to meet R1.
- **Licence:** the repo says "MIT, CC-BY-4.0 licenses found", but the Hugging Face record shows no licence. I believe the data is CC BY 4.0, but that is from memory. Get it in writing before you rely on it.
- **Business fit (R4, from memory):** office-style meetings, but participants were given topics.
- **Access:** use the `download_meeting_subset` function in the repo.

**2. AMI** ([site](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/corpus/))
- **Content:** 100 hours with close-talk and far-field array microphones, and speaker-attributed annotations.
- **Licence:** the official licence page says "released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license". The OpenSLR mirror still lists the old non-commercial CC BY-NC-SA 2.0 licence. Treat the official AMI site as authoritative, and keep a copy of the page in your records.
- **Caveats:** about two-thirds of AMI is role-play, with participants acting as a design team. The rest is naturally occurring meetings. It is also heavily used, so many off-the-shelf models are already tuned to it.

**3. DiPCo** ([Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/8122551))
- **Content:** four Amazon employees having a natural conversation, recorded by five 7-microphone far-field arrays, with human-labelled transcripts.
- **Caveats:** it is small and set at a dinner party, not a meeting. It is useful for far-field robustness, not for business-meeting style.

**4. ICSI Meeting Corpus** ([speech LDC2004S02](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S02), [transcripts LDC2004T04](https://doi.org/10.35111/0sq8-s977))
- **Content:** real research-group meetings with tabletop microphones.
- **Access:** create an LDC account, pay the fee, and ask LDC explicitly about commercial use. The page lists the "LDC User Agreement for Non-Members" but I couldn't read the agreement text.
- **From memory:** ICSI may also host a CC BY 4.0 release. I couldn't reach the ICSI site to confirm.

## Known, not confirmed

- **CHiME-5/6:** real far-field dinner-party data. The official page says "available under licence", and I couldn't confirm the terms. A Hugging Face mirror shows CC BY-SA, but a mirror doesn't set the original terms.
- **Paid vendors** such as Defined.ai, Appen, Speechocean and Nexdata sell licensed multi-speaker English meeting data. I didn't check them. This is probably your best route to business-style, far-field data with a clean commercial licence.

## Not recommended, and why

- **MeetingBank audio:** CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
- **ground-truth/multichannel-meetings-10h:** CC BY-NC 4.0.
- **VoxConverse:** the official site doesn't distribute the audio. It is single-channel YouTube material and not meetings.
- **DIHARD I/II (LDC):** mixed sources rather than meetings, and the commercial terms are unconfirmed.
- **Hugging Face "synthetic" and "simulation" diarization sets:** these are simulated, which fails R1.

## What I could not find

- No large business-meeting corpus with an explicit commercial licence beyond AMI and NOTSOFAR.
- Hugging Face registry search partly failed because the response was too large.

## Next step

1. Start with AMI and NOTSOFAR-1 today, since both are downloadable now.
2. Email Microsoft or check the NOTSOFAR LICENSE files to settle the data licence.
3. Ask LDC about commercial terms for ICSI.
4. Request a quote from a vendor for business-style far-field data. Public sets are modest in size and style.

Page: `/private/tmp/e-b3LFWs/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`

- **Caveats:** about two-thirds of AMI is role-play, with participants acting as a design team. The rest is naturally occurring meetings. It is also heavily used, so many off-the-shelf models are already tuned to it.

**3. DiPCo** ([Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/8122551))
- **Content:** four Amazon employees having a natural conversation, recorded by five 7-microphone far-field arrays, with human-labelled transcripts.
- **Caveats:** it is small and set at a dinner party, not a meeting. It is useful for far-field robustness, not for business-meeting style.

**4. ICSI Meeting Corpus** ([speech LDC2004S02](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S02), [transcripts LDC2004T04](https://doi.org/10.35111/0sq8-s977))
- **Content:** real research-group meetings with tabletop microphones.
- **Access:** create an LDC account, pay the fee, and ask LDC explicitly about commercial use. The page lists the "LDC User Agreement for Non-Members" but I couldn't read the agreement text.
- **From memory:** ICSI may also host a CC BY 4.0 release. I couldn't reach the ICSI site to confirm.

## Known, not confirmed

- **CHiME-5/6:** real far-field dinner-party data. The official page says "available under licence", and I couldn't confirm the terms. A Hugging Face mirror shows CC BY-SA, but a mirror doesn't set the original terms.
- **Paid vendors** such as Defined.ai, Appen, Speechocean and Nexdata sell licensed multi-speaker English meeting data. I didn't check them. This is probably your best route to business-style, far-field data with a clean commercial licence.

## Not recommended, and why

- **MeetingBank audio:** CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
- **ground-truth/multichannel-meetings-10h:** CC BY-NC 4.0.
- **VoxConverse:** the official site doesn't distribute the audio. It is single-channel YouTube material and not meetings.
- **DIHARD I/II (LDC):** mixed sources rather than meetings, and the commercial terms are unconfirmed.
- **Hugging Face "synthetic" and "simulation" diarization sets:** these are simulated, which fails R1.

## What I could not find

- No large business-meeting corpus with an explicit commercial licence beyond AMI and NOTSOFAR.
- Hugging Face registry search partly failed because the response was too large.

## Next step

1. Start with AMI and NOTSOFAR-1 today, since both are downloadable now.
2. Email Microsoft or check the NOTSOFAR LICENSE files to settle the data licence.
3. Ask LDC about commercial terms for ICSI.
4. Request a quote from a vendor for business-style far-field data. Public sets are modest in size and style.

graders.name: 01-recall-ami-meetings
graders.evidence:
**Short list for commercial use:** NOTSOFAR-1, AMI and ICSI cover your requirements. All three are real conversations with far-field audio, speaker annotations and English speech. I'm going from memory, so check each licence on the official page before you commit.

## Core picks

| Corpus | What it is | Far-field / array | Licence (as I recall) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **NOTSOFAR-1** (Microsoft) | About 300 real meetings in office conference rooms, with a range of participant counts and acoustic conditions. It has diarization and transcript annotations. | Yes. It has both single-device and multi-device multichannel recordings. | CC BY 4.0 |
| **AMI Meeting Corpus** | About 100 hours of meetings with headset and 8-channel circular array recordings. It has speaker segmentation and word-level transcripts. | Yes | CC BY 4.0 |
| **ICSI Meeting Corpus** | About 70 hours of naturally occurring research-group meetings. | Tabletop mics plus headsets | I believe CC BY 4.0 now, but confirm. |

- **NOTSOFAR-1** is the closest match to your product and the most recent. It was built for far-field meeting transcription with diarization.
- **AMI** is the standard benchmark, so you can compare your results with published numbers.
  - Roughly two-thirds of it is scenario-driven. Participants play assigned roles in a design team, but the dialogue is unscripted.
  - Many speakers are non-native English speakers, which is useful for robustness.
- **ICSI** is fully natural, but the room is a single setup and the speakers are mostly researchers.

## Smaller or supplementary
- **DiPCo** (Amazon) is about 5 hours of dinner-party conversations recorded with far-field arrays. As I recall it's under a permissive CDLA licence. It's casual rather than business, but it's useful as an extra test set for overlapping speech.
- **LDC meeting corpora** (ISL, NIST meeting room, and similar) are available under LDC licences. LDC has commercial licensing options, and non-members pay fees. This is the "pay a licence fee" route, but the data is old and mostly redundant with AMI and ICSI.

## What to avoid
- **CHiME-6:** I believe its terms are restrictive. Check before using it.
- **VoxConverse, AVA-AVD, MSDWild:** the audio comes from YouTube or film, so the rights are unclear. It's also not far-field meeting audio.
- **LibriCSS and similar:** these are simulated or re-recorded mixtures.
- **Fisher, Switchboard, CallHome:** these are telephone calls, mostly two-party. They're also LDC-licensed.

## Practical notes
1. **Attribution:** CC BY requires credit and a licence notice. It doesn't restrict commercial training or fine-tuning. Keep a data-provenance file listing each source, licence and version.
2. **Consent and privacy:** these corpora were recorded with participant consent, but if you serve EU users, ask counsel about voice data as biometric data.
3. **Size:** about 500 hours total is enough to fine-tune or evaluate diarization models, but not to train one from scratch. Plan on adding your own consented customer or pilot recordings over time.
4. **Evaluation:** hold out NOTSOFAR-1's dev/eval sets and AMI's standard test split so your DER numbers are comparable to published ones.

I can pull up the official licence pages and confirm the exact terms for each one if you'd like.

graders.name: 01-recall-ami-meetings
graders.evidence:
I'm working from memory and haven't checked the current licence pages. Confirm each licence at the source before you commit.

## Best fits

**1. NOTSOFAR-1 (Microsoft, 2024)**
- **Content:** About 450 real, unscripted English meetings of office-style conversation, recorded on multi-channel far-field devices (several mic-array form factors) and on single-channel devices.
- **Annotations:** Speaker-attributed transcripts with timing, so you can derive who spoke when. The recordings were made across many rooms with varied acoustics.
- **Licence:** I recall CC BY 4.0, which allows commercial use with attribution.
- **Caveat:** Participants were recruited and given loose topics, so the meetings are natural but not actual company meetings.
- **Fit:** This is the closest match to your brief. I'd start here.

**2. ICSI Meeting Corpus**
- **Content:** About 75 hours of genuinely naturally occurring research-group meetings, with 4–10 speakers each.
- **Audio:** Close-talk headsets plus tabletop far-field mics.
- **Annotations:** Speaker turns and transcripts.
- **Licence:** I recall CC BY 4.0 via the Edinburgh AMI/ICSI hosting.
- **Caveat:** The content is academic and technical, and the recordings are from the early 2000s.

**3. AMI Meeting Corpus**
- **Content:** About 100 hours of English meetings.
- **Audio:** Headsets, lapel mics, and an 8-channel circular far-field array.
- **Annotations:** Speaker turns, words, and more.
- **Licence:** CC BY 4.0, including the audio, as far as I recall.
- **Caveat:** About two-thirds are role-played "design team" scenarios, with the rest natural meetings. Many speakers are non-native English speakers, which may help or hurt depending on your users.
- **Fit:** It is the standard benchmark, so it's useful for comparing your results with published numbers.

## Worth considering, with licence caveats
- **NIST RT evaluation sets, DIHARD, and similar LDC corpora:** Real meeting and conversational speech with diarization labels. LDC licences are per corpus and per membership tier, and commercial use usually needs a for-profit membership or a separate agreement. Ask LDC before relying on them.
- **DiPCo (Amazon):** Far-field array recordings of dinner-party conversation. I recall a permissive licence (CDLA). The domain is casual conversation, not business.
- **Commercial vendors (Defined.ai, Appen, Speechocean, Shaip):** They can collect or license multi-party, far-field, business-style English meetings with diarization labels and clear commercial rights. This is the route to a paid licence if the open corpora don't match your acoustics or domain.

## Ruled out
- **VoxConverse, AVA-AVD, and other YouTube-derived sets:** The labels may be open, but the underlying audio carries third-party copyright. They also aren't far-field.
- **LibriCSS and other simulated mixtures:** You excluded these.
- **AliMeeting and MISP:** Mandarin, so they don't meet your English-only requirement.
- **CHiME-6:** The licence is restrictive and the domain is dinner parties.

## Suggested approach
1. Use NOTSOFAR-1, AMI, and ICSI together for training and evaluation. They are free for commercial use, with attribution.
2. Hold out part of NOTSOFAR-1 as your primary evaluation set, since it's the most modern and realistic. Report AMI results for comparability.
3. If you need a closer match to your customers' meetings (accents, rooms, domain vocabulary), commission a small paid collection from a vendor, or record consented data from your own pilot customers.

Before shipping, check three things:
- Does the licence cover the audio itself or only the annotations?
- Does it allow training models and distributing them commercially?
- Does the attribution notice appear in your product documentation?

If you'd like, I can fetch the licence pages for these three corpora and confirm the current terms.

FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

graders.name: 01-recall-galaxy-zoo-2
graders.evidence:
## What I assumed you need

- **R1 (must):** at least 40k galaxies.
- **R2 (must):** detailed morphology: bars, spiral arms, bulge size, mergers.
- **R3 (must):** labels from human votes, not model predictions.
- **R4 (nice to have):** images bundled with the labels.
- I assumed a free, direct download and that you'll train on the vote counts or fractions yourself.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Galaxy Zoo 2 (SDSS) images + volunteer table | Open download, minutes | Images CC-BY-4.0. Table terms not checked | 243,434 images (3.35 GB) | Strong | Images: today. Table: today (site text) |
| 2 | Galaxy Zoo DECaLS | Open download, days (~104 GB of images) | CC-BY-4.0 | 314k galaxies in total. Volunteer-labelled subset not counted | Strong | today |
| 3 | Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS (near-infrared) | Open download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | 71,052 galaxies (7.9 GB images) | Partial | today |

## Details

**1. Galaxy Zoo 2**
- **Links:** [images (Zenodo)](https://zenodo.org/records/3565489) and [labels (data.galaxyzoo.org)](https://data.galaxyzoo.org).
- **Contents:** the images come with `gz2_filename_mapping.csv`. The labels are volunteer votes from the GZ2 decision tree, covering bars, spiral arms, bulge prominence and mergers/odd features. They come from 16M classifications. Use the debiased Table 1 (Hart et al. 2016).
- **Why it's first:** it clears 40k comfortably, the labels are human, and the images are lower-resolution SDSS cutouts, a common setting for CNN work.
- **Caveat:** images and labels are two downloads that you join with the mapping file.
- **Zenodo catalogue:** a separate Zenodo copy of the GZ2 catalogue ([record 3566991](https://zenodo.org/records/3566991)) is flagged "restricted". I didn't resolve that. Use data.galaxyzoo.org instead.

**2. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS** ([Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/4573248))
- **Contents:** the record has volunteer-vote files for the GZD-1/2 and GZD-5 campaigns and a `schema.md`. It also has four DR5 PNG image zips, about 104 GB in total. The newer question schema targets mergers and weak bars. Images are higher quality than SDSS.
- **Caveat 1:** the file `gz_decals_auto_posteriors` is *model predictions*. Don't use it as labels. Use only the `gz_decals_volunteers_*` files.
- **Caveat 2:** many GZD-5 galaxies have only about 5 votes, so filter by vote count.
- **Caveat 3:** the record doesn't say how many galaxies have volunteer votes. Count the rows before relying on 40k.

**3. Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS** ([Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/13357341))
- **Contents:** catalogue and images in one record. The catalogue has vote counts and fractions (images are in `ukidss_images.zip`, 7.9 GB).
- **Caveat:** it's near-infrared, so it's less useful as a main training set. It works as a second domain to compare against.

## Known, not confirmed

- **Galaxy Zoo Hubble and CANDELS:** both are listed on data.galaxyzoo.org and have volunteer votes, but I didn't check sizes or whether images are bundled.
- **Euclid Q1 visual morphology catalogue** ([Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/15106473)): I didn't check whether its labels are human or model-derived, or its size.
- **Hugging Face copies** of GZ2 (for example `juliensimon/galaxy-zoo-2-morphology`): they show up as open, but I didn't check which columns they carry. They may be easier to load than the Zenodo zip.

## Not recommended, and why

- **Galaxy Zoo DESI (8.7M):** this is the famous one, but its main catalogue is deep-learning predicted vote fractions, which fails R3. The only human votes in it are about 96k galaxies from the GZD-8 campaign, and the images aren't bundled.
- **Galaxy10 DECaLS:** about 17.7k images (from memory), which is below your 40k, and only 10 coarse classes.
- **Galaxy MNIST:** about 10k images (from memory) and 4 coarse classes. Too small.

## What I could not find

The literature search returned almost nothing relevant, so I found no lesser-known alternatives. The ranking comes from registry searches and the Galaxy Zoo data portal.

## Next step

Download the GZ2 images and Table 1 and join them with the mapping file. Then decide whether the DECaLS vote count is enough to add a second, sharper-image set. This check was done on 2026-11-12, and access terms and versions can change.

The interactive page is at `/private/tmp/e-rixoW4/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Galaxy Zoo 2 (SDSS) images + volunteer table | Open download, minutes | Images CC-BY-4.0. Table terms not checked | 243,434 images (3.35 GB) | Strong | Images: today. Table: today (site text) |
| 2 | Galaxy Zoo DECaLS | Open download, days (~104 GB of images) | CC-BY-4.0 | 314k galaxies in total. Volunteer-labelled subset not counted | Strong | today |
| 3 | Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS (near-infrared) | Open download, minutes | CC-BY-4.0 | 71,052 galaxies (7.9 GB images) | Partial | today |

## Details

**1. Galaxy Zoo 2**
- **Links:** [images (Zenodo)](https://zenodo.org/records/3565489) and [labels (data.galaxyzoo.org)](https://data.galaxyzoo.org).
- **Contents:** the images come with `gz2_filename_mapping.csv`. The labels are volunteer votes from the GZ2 decision tree, covering bars, spiral arms, bulge prominence and mergers/odd features. They come from 16M classifications. Use the debiased Table 1 (Hart et al. 2016).
- **Why it's first:** it clears 40k comfortably, the labels are human, and the images are lower-resolution SDSS cutouts, a common setting for CNN work.
- **Caveat:** images and labels are two downloads that you join with the mapping file.
- **Zenodo catalogue:** a separate Zenodo copy of the GZ2 catalogue ([record 3566991](https://zenodo.org/records/3566991)) is flagged "restricted". I didn't resolve that. Use data.galaxyzoo.org instead.

**2. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS** ([Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/4573248))
- **Contents:** the record has volunteer-vote files for the GZD-1/2 and GZD-5 campaigns and a `schema.md`. It also has four DR5 PNG image zips, about 104 GB in total. The newer question schema targets mergers and weak bars. Images are higher quality than SDSS.
- **Caveat 1:** the file `gz_decals_auto_posteriors` is *model predictions*. Don't use it as labels. Use only the `gz_decals_volunteers_*` files.
- **Caveat 2:** many GZD-5 galaxies have only about 5 votes, so filter by vote count.
- **Caveat 3:** the record doesn't say how many galaxies have volunteer votes. Count the rows before relying on 40k.

**3. Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS** ([Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/13357341))
- **Contents:** catalogue and images in one record. The catalogue has vote counts and fractions (images are in `ukidss_images.zip`, 7.9 GB).
- **Caveat:** it's near-infrared, so it's less useful as a main training set. It works as a second domain to compare against.

## Known, not confirmed

- **Galaxy Zoo Hubble and CANDELS:** both are listed on data.galaxyzoo.org and have volunteer votes, but I didn't check sizes or whether images are bundled.
- **Euclid Q1 visual morphology catalogue** ([Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/15106473)): I didn't check whether its labels are human or model-derived, or its size.
- **Hugging Face copies** of GZ2 (for example `juliensimon/galaxy-zoo-2-morphology`): they show up as open, but I didn't check which columns they carry. They may be easier to load than the Zenodo zip.

- **Galaxy Zoo DESI (8.7M):** this is the famous one, but its main catalogue is deep-learning predicted vote fractions, which fails R3. The only human votes in it are about 96k galaxies from the GZD-8 campaign, and the images aren't bundled.
- **Galaxy10 DECaLS:** about 17.7k images (from memory), which is below your 40k, and only 10 coarse classes.
- **Galaxy MNIST:** about 10k images (from memory) and 4 coarse classes. Too small.

The literature search returned almost nothing relevant, so I found no lesser-known alternatives. The ranking comes from registry searches and the Galaxy Zoo data portal.

Download the GZ2 images and Table 1 and join them with the mapping file. Then decide whether the DECaLS vote count is enough to add a second, sharper-image set. This check was done on 2026-11-12, and access terms and versions can change.

The interactive page is at `/private/tmp/e-rixoW4/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.
