- **Size (must):** at least 40k human-labelled galaxies.
- **Cost (must):** free.
- **Images (nice to have):** images bundled with the labels.
- **Assumption:** you are fine joining a vote table to an image folder yourself.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (GZD-1/2/5 volunteer catalogues) | Open download, minutes to days (large files) | CC-BY-4.0 | 314k galaxies in the record; the human-labelled count is not stated | Strong | Today |
| 2 | Galaxy Zoo 2, original-sample images (+ vote tables from data.galaxyzoo.org) | Open download | Images CC-BY-4.0; table terms not checked | ~240k galaxies (from memory) | Strong | Images today; tables from memory |
| 3 | Galaxy Zoo: Cosmic Dawn (Euclid Deep Field North) | Open download | CC-BY-4.0 | "Over 41,000" galaxies | Strong, but borderline on size | Today |
| 4 | Galaxy Zoo DESI, GZD-8 volunteer subset only | Open download | CC-BY-4.0 | 96k galaxies | Partial (no images) | Today |
| 5 | Galaxy10 DECaLS | Open download | CC-BY-4.0 | ~18k | Partial (too small) | Today |

## Details

**1. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS** — https://zenodo.org/records/4573248
- It has volunteer vote counts from the GZD-1/2 and GZD-5 campaigns. The GZD-5 schema was "designed to better detect mergers and weak bars".
- It also includes the GZD-5 images that volunteers saw.
- Use only the volunteer files (`gz_decals_volunteers_1_and_2` and `gz_decals_volunteers_5`). `gz_decals_auto_posteriors` is model output.
- Many GZD-5 galaxies have only about 5 votes, so filter on vote count.
- The full record is about 108 GB. The page says the large image files may be hosted at the University of Manchester while Zenodo upload is pending.
- Images for GZD-1/2 are not bundled. You would fetch them from the Legacy Survey.

**2. Galaxy Zoo 2** — images: https://zenodo.org/records/3565489 (3.4 GB)
- The images are the original GZ2 sample. The record's own example is a galaxy volunteers called "a barred spiral galaxy with a mild bulge and two tightly-wound arms".
- The vote tables are on data.galaxyzoo.org (Willett et al. 2013; debiased version in Hart et al. 2016). The tool could only reach that site's home page, so I haven't confirmed the table files or their terms. Your join key is the SDSS object ID.
- SDSS images are lower resolution than DECaLS.
- Rotation-invariant CNNs trained on GZ2 labels are well established (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stv632).

**3. Galaxy Zoo: Cosmic Dawn** — https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17200992
- This is the only one where images and volunteer labels sit in the same record (PNG/JPG images plus `gzcd_volunteer_classifications.parquet`).
- It also contains Zoobot predictions, so use only the volunteer file.
- 41k leaves little room once you cut by vote count.
- The galaxies are deeper and higher-redshift than SDSS, so the domain differs.

**4. Galaxy Zoo DESI, GZD-8 only** — https://zenodo.org/records/8360385
- Use only `gz_desi_gzd8_volunteer_core_catalog.parquet` and the extended catalogue. These hold votes for 96k galaxies.
- The 8.7M-galaxy catalogues are deep-learning predictions.
- No images are included. Cut out Legacy Survey images by position.

**5. Galaxy10 DECaLS** — https://zenodo.org/records/10845026 (also on Hugging Face as `mwalmsley/galaxy10_decals`)
- It is the only ready-to-use images-plus-labels bundle, and its labels come from volunteer votes.
- It has about 18k images in 10 broad classes, so it is under your minimum. Use it for a quick baseline.

**What I'd do:** combine #1 (GZD-5, which has bundled images) and #4 (GZD-8 volunteer votes, 96k galaxies, images from the Legacy Survey). Both use the same DECaLS imaging and the same question tree. That gives you well over 40k human-labelled galaxies with bars, arms, bulge and merger questions.

## Known, not confirmed

- **GZ2 vote tables at data.galaxyzoo.org.** I believe they are open, but I couldn't check the files or licence today.
- **Volunteer-labelled count in GZ DECaLS.** The record doesn't state it. Count the rows in the volunteer catalogues before relying on it.

## Not recommended, and why

- **Euclid Q1 visual morphology catalogue** (https://zenodo.org/records/15106473). It has images and a large catalogue, but the page says the measurements "were made by Zoobot foundation models". These are model predictions, which you ruled out.
- **Galaxy Zoo DESI main catalogues (8.7M).** These are predicted vote fractions.
- **Galaxy10 SDSS.** It has 21.8k images at 69×69 pixels, which is below your minimum and low resolution.

## What I could not find

- A single download that bundles images and human-only labels at 40k or more.
- I did not look at Hubble or CANDELS Galaxy Zoo, or Radio Galaxy Zoo, which may offer more.
- The "papers that used it" check returned only one clearly relevant paper.

## Next step

Download the GZD-8 volunteer catalogue (#4) and the GZD-5 volunteer catalogue (#1). Count galaxies with at least about 10 votes per question, then fetch images for those.

Checked on 2026-11-11. Access rules and licences can change.

Interactive page: `/private/tmp/e-NBkNNi/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`

graders.name: 01-recall-galaxy-zoo-2
graders.evidence:
I'd start with **Galaxy Zoo**. It's the main source of volunteer-labelled galaxy morphology. These are the options that fit your constraints (I'm going from memory, so check the exact sizes and URLs on the pages).

## Best fits

**1. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (GZD-5, and GZD-8 in the later releases)**
- It has hundreds of thousands of galaxies (roughly 250k for GZD-5). The images are deeper and sharper than SDSS.
- The labels are volunteer vote counts for a decision tree. It covers bars, spiral arm count and tightness, bulge size, mergers and tidal features, edge-on discs, and more.
- Walmsley et al. 2022 describes it.
- The Zoobot project (Walmsley et al.) hosts the images and votes together on Hugging Face under the `mwalmsley` account, so you can load them with the `datasets` library. Search for the `gz_decals` and `gz_evo` datasets.

**2. Galaxy Zoo 2 (SDSS)**
- It has about 240k to 300k galaxies in the Willett et al. 2013 catalogue, with vote fractions on the same kind of questions: bar, spiral, bulge prominence (none, just noticeable, obvious, dominant), merger or odd features, and edge-on.
- The images are lower resolution than DECaLS. They are 424×424 JPEGs.
- The **Kaggle "Galaxy Zoo – The Galaxy Challenge"** download bundles about 61k training images with 37 vote-fraction columns. That is above your 40k minimum, and the images and labels come together. You need a free Kaggle account and have to accept the competition rules.
- The Hugging Face `gz2` dataset is another option.

## What to avoid

- **Galaxy10 DECaLS and Galaxy10 SDSS** are convenient, but they're too small (about 17k and 21k). They also reduce the votes to 10 coarse classes, so you'd lose bar, bulge and merger detail.
- **Galaxy Zoo DESI** and parts of **GZ Evo** mix volunteer votes with Zoobot model predictions. This matters because you need human-only labels. If you use them, take only the volunteer vote-count columns and ignore the model-posterior columns. For a clean thesis, GZD-5 or GZ2 is simpler to defend.

## Using the votes

- **Filter by vote count.** Keep galaxies where the relevant question has at least about 20 to 30 votes. Questions are conditional, so a bar vote only exists for galaxies that volunteers called "featured, not edge-on".
- **Train on vote fractions or counts** (soft labels or a Dirichlet/multinomial loss) rather than hard classes. Zoobot does this.
- **Check class balance.** Mergers and strong bars are rare, so you'll need weighting or oversampling.
- **Cite the papers** (Willett 2013, Walmsley 2022, and the Galaxy Zoo volunteers). Both data releases ask for this.

I'd go with GZD-5 from Hugging Face for the main run, and use the Kaggle GZ2 set as a second dataset to test generalisation across surveys. I can write the download and filtering script if you want.

graders.name: 01-recall-galaxy-zoo-2
graders.evidence:
**Recommendation: Galaxy Zoo.** Its labels are volunteer votes, and the sets are large enough for your 40k minimum. I'm going from memory and haven't checked the repositories or licences, so confirm exact names and terms before you build on them.

## Best options

**1. Galaxy Zoo 2 (SDSS), about 240k–300k galaxies**
- **Labels:** the volunteers answered a decision tree covering bar (strong, weak or none), spiral arms (present, how many, how tightly wound), bulge size (none, just noticeable, obvious, dominant), edge-on or not, and odd features such as mergers, irregulars and disturbed galaxies. This matches the labels you listed.
- **Images with labels bundled:** the Kaggle "Galaxy Zoo – The Galaxy Challenge" set has 61,578 labelled 424×424 JPEGs. Each has 37 vote-fraction columns from GZ2. That clears 40k and is the quickest way to start.
- **Full catalogue:** the GZ2 data release (Willett et al. 2013) has the vote counts for the whole sample. You would match it to SDSS cutouts yourself.

**2. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (DESI Legacy Surveys), about 300k galaxies**
- Its images are deeper and sharper than SDSS, and its question tree is similar. It adds finer merger and disturbance questions and tidal features.
- Releases from Walmsley et al. are mirrored on Hugging Face (look under the `mwalmsley` account, e.g. the `gz_*` datasets) with images and labels together. Check the exact repo names there.

## What to avoid
- **Galaxy10 DECaLS (~17.7k) and Galaxy10 SDSS (~21k):** both are built from volunteer votes, but they are too small. They also collapse the labels into 10 coarse classes, which loses the bar, bulge and arm detail you want.
- **Galaxy Zoo DESI and Euclid releases:** these catalogues mix raw volunteer votes with predictions from the Zoobot model for galaxies that were never classified. If you use them, keep only galaxies with real vote counts. Otherwise you break your human-labels-only rule.

## Practical caveats
- **Labels are vote fractions, not hard classes.** Filter on the number of votes and on a vote-fraction threshold, for example p > 0.8 with at least 10–20 votes on that question. Otherwise you train on noisy labels.
- **Classes are imbalanced.** Mergers and strong bars are rare, so plan for weighting or resampling.
- **Questions depend on earlier answers.** Bar and spiral-arm votes only apply if the galaxy was marked as featured and not edge-on. Apply those parent-question filters.
- **Check the licence and citation terms.** Kaggle competition data comes with its own rules and needs an account. Galaxy Zoo asks you to cite the relevant papers.

If you want one download, take the Kaggle GZ2 set. If you want better image quality and finer merger labels, take GZ DECaLS from Hugging Face.

- **Full catalogue:** the GZ2 data release (Willett et al. 2013) has the vote counts for the whole sample. You would match it to SDSS cutouts yourself.

**2. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (DESI Legacy Surveys), about 300k galaxies**
- Its images are deeper and sharper than SDSS, and its question tree is similar. It adds finer merger and disturbance questions and tidal features.
- Releases from Walmsley et al. are mirrored on Hugging Face (look under the `mwalmsley` account, e.g. the `gz_*` datasets) with images and labels together. Check the exact repo names there.

## What to avoid
- **Galaxy10 DECaLS (~17.7k) and Galaxy10 SDSS (~21k):** both are built from volunteer votes, but they are too small. They also collapse the labels into 10 coarse classes, which loses the bar, bulge and arm detail you want.
- **Galaxy Zoo DESI and Euclid releases:** these catalogues mix raw volunteer votes with predictions from the Zoobot model for galaxies that were never classified. If you use them, keep only galaxies with real vote counts. Otherwise you break your human-labels-only rule.

## Practical caveats
- **Labels are vote fractions, not hard classes.** Filter on the number of votes and on a vote-fraction threshold, for example p > 0.8 with at least 10–20 votes on that question. Otherwise you train on noisy labels.
- **Classes are imbalanced.** Mergers and strong bars are rare, so plan for weighting or resampling.
- **Questions depend on earlier answers.** Bar and spiral-arm votes only apply if the galaxy was marked as featured and not edge-on. Apply those parent-question filters.
- **Check the licence and citation terms.** Kaggle competition data comes with its own rules and needs an account. Galaxy Zoo asks you to cite the relevant papers.

If you want one download, take the Kaggle GZ2 set. If you want better image quality and finer merger labels, take GZ DECaLS from Hugging Face.
